dominant_strengths: Conceptually novel: an LLM-targeted machine-readable doc page is a clever AEO/agent-era artifact for fintech distribution
Clear semantic hierarchy via markdown headings makes parsing trivial for both agents and skimming humans
Information density is high yet logically chunked into Offer, Overview, and Core Products sections
dominant_weaknesses: Visual presentation is raw terminal markdown — no Ramp brand expression, no typographic rhythm, no color system
Monospaced wall of text with green-on-black ANSI vibe feels generic and undermines Ramp's premium fintech identity
Zero spatial composition: no grid, no whitespace strategy, no visual anchors to guide attention to the $3,100 offer
fix_priorities: Render the markdown with Ramp's actual brand typography and palette so machine-readability and brand equity coexist
Introduce a visual hierarchy treatment for the offer block (callout, border, accent color) to anchor the page
Add structured metadata styling (definition lists, tables) instead of bold-prefix prose for cleaner scanability
Tighten line-length and vertical rhythm — current 1500px-wide monospace lines fatigue any human reader
rationale.norman_balance: Heavy reflective/behavioral lean (clever agent-targeting concept, functional info delivery) with near-zero visceral payoff due to unstyled terminal aesthetic.
rationale.intent_fit: It serves the Ramp brief functionally as an AI-agent-facing spec, but as a 'fintech design' artifact it abdicates visual craft entirely.
